number of cases in each individual rectangle.  You can use

the total count, so it doesn't change the appearance of the plot at
all, only the value range on the colorbar.

What would I have to do to get the fill to be proportional to the
density within _each vertical strip considered by itself_?  That might
be easier to understand with an example: given prebinned data

test.d <- data.frame(x=c(1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3), y=c(1,2,3,1,2,3,1,2,3),
count=c(12,6,3,4,2,0,1,0,0))

fill=..density.. effectively does

test.d$density <-  test.d$count / sum(test.d$count)

but the calculation I want is

test.d$v.density <- ddply(test.d, .(x), function(blk)
data.frame(v.density=blk$count / sum(blk$count)))$v.density

However, I do _not_ have pre-binned data so I need to persuade
stat_bin2d to do that somehow.

zw

In case anybody hits this thread by googling, the key point seems to be to set xmin and xmax (i.e. outside aes()) while mapping ymin and ymax (i.e. inside aes()) if necessary…
works with ggplot2_2.2.1 (and probably earlier).

data<-data.frame(name=c("a", "b", "c", "d"), mean=c(5, 9, 7, 11), se=c(1.2, 0.9, 3, 2))
ggplot()+
  #layer creating a rectangle across the plot

  geom_rect(data=data[data$name=="b",], xmin=-Inf, xmax=Inf, aes(ymin=mean-se, ymax=mean+se), fill='white', alpha=0.8)+

  geom_pointrange(data=data, aes(x=reorder(name, mean), y=mean, ymin=mean-se, ymax=mean+se))+

  labs(y="b*")

Hadley and Stefanie,

Yes, that does correct the issue:

ggplot(forggplot, aes(reorder(cytokine, percent_res), percent_res, group = cytokine, label = percent_res))+
    geom_line(aes(colour = responseType)) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = responseType, shape = MSD), size = 6) +

    geom_text(color = 'white', size = 2)    +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22)) +

    scale_color_manual(values = c('#1b9e77', '#d95f02', '#7570b3', '#66a61e')

                            , labels = c('antiinflam', 'Th1', 'Th2', 'Th17')
                            , name = 'Category') +

    scale_fill_manual(values = c('#1b9e77', '#d95f02', '#7570b3', '#66a61e')

                            , labels = c('antiinflam', 'Th1', 'Th2', 'Th17')
                            , name = 'Category') +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_bw() +

    labs(x = 'Cytokine',
       y = '% responders',
       title = paste('Percent responders')) +

    theme(axis.text = element_text(face = 'bold')) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21)))

You can specify color or fill or both and all of those print the plot as desired.

HTH,
B
